01 / HOW LLMS WORK

A mental model.
Before the actual model.

Training learns patterns. Inference uses them.

TRAINING

Labeled emails → learned patterns

Classic machine learning learns from examples, such as emails labeled “spam” or “not spam.”

INFERENCE

New email → prediction

The trained model applies those patterns to a new email: for example, “Spam (94%).”

The right tool depends on the task

Rules or classic ML often beat LLMs on narrow, repetitive tasks with lots of labeled data, or when speed, low cost, consistency, and exact arithmetic matter. Exact calculations belong in rules or code.

INSIDE THE LOOP

One token at a time.

ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO

An LLM splits text into tokens, predicts a next token, adds it to the context, and repeats. Tokens can be words, parts of words, or punctuation.

ThecapitalofFranceis?

Context is ready. What comes next?

A simplified, scripted illustration, not a live model or tokenizer. Actual token boundaries depend on the model.
It generates plausible text.
Plausible ≠ true.

What the model sees

TRAINING KNOWLEDGE

What it learned before

Bounded by its training and knowledge cutoff.

+
CONTEXT WINDOW

What it sees right now

The information supplied in the current interaction.

Don’t assume a model knows your client’s data or last week’s news. Relevant information must reach it through context, including any connected tools or retrieval.

02 / BREAKING THE MODEL

Find the failure.
Design the defense.

Fluency is easy to mistake for reliability. Know what can go wrong.

01HallucinationConfident, fluent, and wrong+

A convincing answer can contain invented or unsupported claims.

Defense: Ground answers in sources and verify citations. Week 7

02InconsistencySame prompt, different answers+

The same request can produce different outputs or judgments.

Defense: Clear prompts and human review of ambiguous cases. Weeks 3, 8

03Unreliable mathGenerating digits isn’t calculating+

Text generation alone is not a reliable calculator.

Defense: Send calculations to code and check the results. Weeks 4, 6

04Character-level errorsIDs and exact strings get mangled+

Token-level patterns can make exact character handling unreliable. Inspect important identifiers against the original source.

Full example: invoice matching at Hearthstone +

Hearthstone Home Goods is a fictional retailer. Its accounts payable team matches approximately 800 vendor invoices a month to purchase orders before paying.

SubtaskApproachWhy
Pull vendor, invoice number, line items, and total from PDFsCombinationAn LLM handles varied layouts; code checks that line items add up to the total.
Match vendor names to the vendor listCombinationFuzzy-matching code first; an LLM suggests leftovers; a human confirms.
Compare invoice totals to PO amountsRules / codeRequires exact arithmetic.
Flag possible duplicate invoicesRules / codeSame number, vendor, and amount is a simple, testable rule.
Explain each mismatch in plain EnglishLLMSummarizing is a strength; text is reviewed before use.
Approve payment on mismatches over $5,000HumanFinancial accountability can’t be delegated to a model.

Biggest risk

Extraction misreads $12,450 as $1,245 and a wrong payment goes through. Code re-adds the line items and routes any disagreement to a human review queue.

Example evidence statement

“In our class test, the model’s sum of 20 dollar amounts was wrong, so all amount comparisons stay in code.”

This statement comes from the deck’s example deliverable. Replace it with your own observed result; it is not a reported test from this website.
